# =============================================================================
# config/source-registry.yaml — SCHEMA V2 (N9 build; gate source-registry-v2,
# SIGNED OFF 2026-07-31 — D1–D4 + Q1–Q6, config/gate-log.md).
#
# TWO LEVELS (D1): a SYSTEM row is the thing we connect to (connection,
# locator, classification, SDLC link); a DATASET row is the thing a loader
# reads and a gate rules (feeds_taxonomy, crosswalk, confirmed — each dataset
# carries its OWN confirmed state). Loaders bind to DATASET ids
# (BaseLoader.source_id), overridable per repo by
# config/loader-source-overlay.yaml (D2 — the T19 rebind seam).
#
# ID GRAMMAR (Q1, amended at the gate):
#   system  id:  {system}                        e.g. psgmgr, seal, pat, snow
#   dataset id:  {origin}@{db}.{schema}.{table}  replica/derived — the segment
#                after @ is the ACTUAL qualified carrier locator (it REPLACES
#                the informal system nickname); lowercase; real db/schema
#                values are connection coordinates -> internal twin only, so
#                committed ids carry [db] (and [schema] where the schema name
#                is not established public vocabulary — psgmgr is)
#                {system}:{artifact}             born-here datasets
#   Derived stores keep the @ grammar + `derived: true`; `authority` is
#   omitted there (Q3 — not SOR/ADS; FCDO SOC = upstream capture, doesn't fit).
#
# AUTHORITY (FCDO vocabulary as a FIELD): SOR = originating source for this
# set of data; ADS = approved copy/redistribution carrier. Attaches to the
# DATASET, never the system (their own definition is per-data-subset).
#
# URN (D3 + Q2): urn:drydocs:dataset:({carrier-or-origin},{artifact},prod) —
# DERIVED by drydocs_core/source_registry.py from the row's system + artifact,
# lowercase, env always prod. NEVER hand-maintained: a row carrying `urn:` is
# refused at parse time.
#
# RETIRED IDS (D4): every legacy v1 flat id lands below with its replacement;
# SourceRegistry.from_yaml AND the overlay guard REFUSE any retired id — a
# retired string can never be silently re-minted with a different meaning
# (the catalog-pat / pat-catalog T19 collision class). Renamed rows carry
# `replaces:` back-pointers.
#
# DOC CORPORA live in config/doc-source-registry.yaml ONLY (the twins dropped
# at N9; one home per source). The runtime SourceRegistry is the UNION of the
# two ledgers, so the confirmed-gate still guards doc loads. design-docs is
# pipeline-side only (Q5 — it feeds graph classes beyond Document/Chunk).
#
# REQUIRED (enforced by tests/unit/test_classification.py):
#   system rows:  classification (config/classification.yaml level) + name
#   dataset rows: system (resolving to a system row) + artifact
#   seal_id is a STANDING PLACEHOLDER on every committed system row (D1
#   amendment) — the real value lives only in the internal/ twin.
#
# MIGRATION NOTE (the N7 residual, executed 2026-07-31): every v1 row was
# confirmed PER ROW at this build. Rows whose gates were signed transfer
# `confirmed: true` per Q6 (one gate-log amendment maps old->new ids);
# everything else lands `confirmed: false`. The split also RECORDS states the
# flat v1 rows could not: cm_avg_run is now visibly unconfirmed (its gate
# controlm-avg-run-supplement is still AWAITING SME) even though the old
# controlm-psgmgr umbrella row read `confirmed: true`.
# =============================================================================

schema: drydocs.source-registry.v2
updated: 2026-07-31

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SYSTEMS — the things we connect to. layer = BDAT four-value view
# (human | business | data | technology; gate ruling 2026-07-31). cmdb_ci is
# the ServiceNow class crosswalk hook — values land at the crosswalk gate once
# snow:cmdb-ci-classes is confirmed (Q4); until then `~`.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
systems:
  - id: psgmgr
    name: "psgmgr Control-M replica DB (Oracle)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"                # PLACEHOLDER — real value internal/ twin only (D1 amendment)
    cmdb_ci: ~                          # crosswalk source = snow:cmdb-ci-classes (Q4); value lands at that gate
    layer: data
    classification: Internal            # operational scheduling metadata; not for public GitHub
    locator:
      platform: oracle-db               # what CARRIES it — software-registry product id
      service: ~                        # DB service/TNS — connection env (internal-local/), never committed
      schema: psgmgr                    # established public vocabulary
    sdlc: docs/reviews/sdlc-oracle-ingestion.md
    notes: >
      The Control-M replica database — CARRIER, not origin: Control-M data
      (origin controlm) and SEAL data (origin seal) both land here as replica
      datasets; the v2 grammar makes that visible where the old flat
      controlm-psgmgr id hid it.

  - id: controlm
    name: "BMC Control-M (the orchestrator itself)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: technology
    classification: Internal
    locator:
      source_product: controlm          # config/taxonomy/software-registry.yaml product id
    sdlc: ~
    notes: >
      The ORIGIN system for every controlm@... replica dataset and for the
      born-here XML definition export. Version 9.0.21.300 company-side
      (XML-not-JSON finding — the JSON Automation API is conceptual reference).

  - id: seal
    name: "SEAL application inventory"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: business
    classification: Internal            # confidential handling: real applications, ownership, employees, SEAL ids
    locator: {}
    sdlc: ~
    notes: "Applications + ownership; SOR for the application/org datasets."

  - id: pat
    name: "Product Agility Tool (internal catalog UI)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: business
    classification: Internal            # confidential handling: real LOB→Product→Team rosters, team names, SEAL ids
    locator:
      source_product: pat
    sdlc: ~
    notes: >
      LOB→Product→Team catalog (lowest precedence authority). The T19 naming
      ruling lives on its datasets: neither legacy string (catalog-pat /
      pat-catalog) survives — see the retired list.

  - id: snow
    name: "ServiceNow (SaaS ITSM / CMDB)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: technology
    classification: Internal
    locator:
      hosting: saas                     # Q4 ruling 2026-07-31: registers NOW, typed SaaS
    sdlc: ~
    notes: >
      Registered at the N7 gate (Q4). First dataset = snow:cmdb-ci-classes,
      which doubles as the crosswalk source for every system row's cmdb_ci
      field.

  - id: autosys
    name: "AutoSys (CA/Broadcom) — placeholder orchestrator"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: technology
    classification: Internal
    locator: {}
    sdlc: ~
    notes: "Crosswalk-only activation; no export feed exists (external/orchestration/autosys/)."

  - id: airflow
    name: "AWS Airflow / MWAA — placeholder orchestrator"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: technology
    classification: Internal
    locator: {}
    sdlc: ~
    notes: "Crosswalk-only activation; no DAG-export feed exists (external/orchestration/airflow/)."

  - id: dpl
    name: "DPL pipeline/dataset taxonomy registry"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: technology
    classification: Internal            # confidential handling: real SEAL ids + pipeline/dataset GUIDs
    locator:
      data_root: "DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT (default ~/data/DryDocs); dpl-registry/<seal>/ = per-SEAL exports"
      resolver: drydocs_core/data_root.py   # dpl_registry_dir() (the G19 shared helper)
    sdlc: ~
    notes: >
      THE POINTER, NEVER THE DATA: per-SEAL Swagger exports carry real SEAL
      ids, GUIDs and lifecycle state and never enter the repo tree; fixtures
      are SYNTHETIC (G25).

  - id: snowflake
    name: "Snowflake (data platform)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: data
    classification: Internal
    locator: {}
    sdlc: ~
    notes: "Carrier for the catalog@... registration views; per-schema data expansion is a future gate."

  - id: catalog
    name: "Enterprise data catalog (dataset/distribution registration)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: data
    classification: Internal            # confidential handling: real dataset names, GUIDs, app ids, contacts, buckets, URIs
    locator:
      data_root: "DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT (default ~/data/DryDocs); catalog/ = view exports, catalog/screenshots/ = evidence captures (confidential, never in-tree even gitignored)"
      resolver: drydocs_core/data_root.py   # catalog_dir() (the G19 shared helper)
    sdlc: ~
    notes: >
      The registration system whose curated views we read FROM Snowflake (the
      carrier) — origin catalog, carrier snowflake, exactly the replica case
      the @ grammar exists for (G42 seam).

  - id: exec-hosts
    name: "Control-M execution hosts (rua collector)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: technology
    classification: Internal            # confidential handling: bundles hold real hostnames, uids, home paths, script copies
    locator:
      data_root: "DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT (default ~/data/DryDocs); rua/incoming/ = tarballs, rua/extracted/<bundle>/ = unpacked"
      resolver: drydocs_core/data_root.py   # the ONE shared helper (G19)
    sdlc: ~
    notes: >
      THE POINTER, NEVER THE DATA: bundle payloads are confidential and never
      enter the repo tree (guard: tests/unit/test_data_root.py); transport is
      the internal-local hand-carry note (G19).

  - id: bitbucket
    name: "Company code repositories (Bitbucket/GitHub)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: technology
    classification: Internal            # real repo/branch names + script paths; content stays company-side
    locator: {}
    sdlc: ~
    notes: >
      A repo is a valid truth source ONLY where a team keeps a clean branch
      (trusted_ref on the dataset row); production servers always run the
      latest RUNNING code (G24).

  - id: oracle
    name: "Oracle DB schemas (data platform, placeholder)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: data
    classification: Internal            # confidential handling: real schema/table/object names
    locator: {}
    sdlc: ~
    notes: "Per-schema system split + datasets per table group are a future gate (migration sketch row)."

  - id: drydocs-stg
    name: "DryDocs staging schema (our own derived store)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: data
    classification: Internal
    locator:
      schema: drydocs_stg               # our own staging schema (mechanism; committed in v1 too)
    sdlc: docs/reviews/sdlc-oracle-ingestion.md
    notes: "Holds the C3/C4 normalizer outputs (derived stores — Q3: derived: true, authority omitted)."

  - id: repo
    name: "The DryDocs repo itself (repo-committed ledgers + derived captures)"
    seal_id: "[seal-id]"
    cmdb_ci: ~
    layer: technology
    classification: Internal-Public     # the repo's own committed artifacts; per-dataset notes tighten where needed
    locator: {}
    sdlc: ~
    notes: "Born-here datasets: the software-registry ledger, depgraph snapshots, design docs (tenant 0)."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DATASETS — what loaders read and gates rule. `confirmed` is PER DATASET.
# `urn` is DERIVED (never written here). `replaces` back-points the retired
# v1 flat id (D4).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
datasets:
  # ---- Control-M replica datasets in psgmgr (origin controlm = SOR, carrier
  # ---- psgmgr = ADS). Column ledger: config/source-mappings/psgmgr.yaml.
  - id: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_def_vtab"
    system: psgmgr
    origin: controlm
    artifact: cm_def_vtab
    artifact_kind: table
    taxonomy_category: Pipelines
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: ADS
    feeds_taxonomy: [folders]
    adapter: oracle
    locator:
      mapping: config/source-mappings/psgmgr.yaml
    confirmed: true                     # gate controlm-q1q3-phase1 (2026-07-07) — transfers per Q6
    replaces: controlm-psgmgr
    notes: >
      Folders (replicated DEF_VTAB). Loader controlm_folders.v1 (+ the
      CM_DEF_VJOB folder HEADER ROW join for APPLICATION — gate q1q3 §Q3).

  - id: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_def_vjob"
    system: psgmgr
    origin: controlm
    artifact: cm_def_vjob
    artifact_kind: table
    taxonomy_category: Pipelines
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: ADS
    feeds_taxonomy: [jobs]
    adapter: oracle
    locator:
      mapping: config/source-mappings/psgmgr.yaml
    confirmed: true                     # gate controlm-q1q3-phase1 (2026-07-07) — transfers per Q6
    replaces: controlm-psgmgr
    notes: >
      Job definitions — the SME's own worked example for the amended Q1
      grammar (controlm@[db].[schema].cm_def_vjob). Audit envelope confirmed
      (config/audit-fields.yaml). job.APPLICATION is NOT reliable SEAL
      identity (K1) — SEAL attribution rides the stg_app_fact dataset.

  - id: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_def_lnki_p_vw"
    system: psgmgr
    origin: controlm
    artifact: cm_def_lnki_p_vw
    artifact_kind: view
    taxonomy_category: Pipelines
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: ADS
    feeds_taxonomy: [conditions, dependencies]
    adapter: oracle
    locator:
      mapping: config/source-mappings/psgmgr.yaml
    confirmed: true                     # gate controlm-q1q3-phase1 (2026-07-07) — transfers per Q6
    replaces: controlm-psgmgr
    notes: >
      IN-conditions. Also the anchor dataset for the derived WAS_INFORMED_BY
      pairing (controlm_dependencies_derived.v1 joins this view to the OUT
      view on condition name — recorded here, per-row residual 2026-07-31).

  - id: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_def_lnko_p_vw"
    system: psgmgr
    origin: controlm
    artifact: cm_def_lnko_p_vw
    artifact_kind: view
    taxonomy_category: Pipelines
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: ADS
    feeds_taxonomy: [conditions]
    adapter: oracle
    locator:
      mapping: config/source-mappings/psgmgr.yaml
    confirmed: true                     # gate controlm-q1q3-phase1 (2026-07-07) — transfers per Q6
    replaces: controlm-psgmgr
    notes: "OUT-conditions."

  - id: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_def_setvar_vw"
    system: psgmgr
    origin: controlm
    artifact: cm_def_setvar_vw
    artifact_kind: view
    taxonomy_category: Pipelines
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: ADS
    feeds_taxonomy: [variables]
    adapter: oracle
    locator:
      mapping: config/source-mappings/psgmgr.yaml
    confirmed: true                     # covered by controlm-q1q3-phase1 (the five psgmgr extracts) + the C3/C4 normalization gates — transfers per Q6
    replaces: controlm-psgmgr
    notes: >
      Folder/job variables — the C3/C4 Python-normalizer input feeding the
      derived stg_app_fact dataset. No direct graph loader; Python owns var
      resolution.

  - id: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_hosts"
    system: psgmgr
    origin: controlm
    artifact: cm_hosts
    artifact_kind: table
    taxonomy_category: Infrastructure
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: ADS
    feeds_taxonomy: [hosts]
    adapter: oracle
    locator:
      mapping: config/source-mappings/psgmgr.yaml
    confirmed: true                     # gate controlm-hosts-topology (2026-07-09); hosts loader + RUNS_ON shipped at P3 (2026-07-27) — transfers per Q6
    replaces: controlm-psgmgr
    notes: "Host-group membership (added 2026-07-09 via add-source-object)."

  - id: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_avg_run"
    system: psgmgr
    origin: controlm
    artifact: cm_avg_run
    artifact_kind: table
    taxonomy_category: Pipelines
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: ADS
    feeds_taxonomy: [runtime_stats]
    adapter: oracle
    locator:
      mapping: config/source-mappings/psgmgr.yaml
    confirmed: true                     # gate controlm-avg-run-supplement SIGNED OFF 2026-07-14 (P2; 20 confirmations, §B ctlm_id join edit) — transfers per Q6. The v1 umbrella row's note still read "AWAITING SME": stale since 07-14, caught at this per-row confirmation sweep.
    replaces: controlm-psgmgr
    notes: >
      Runtime stats (avg/median start+run) — property supplement onto
      :ControlMJob, no new vocabulary (MATCH-never-MERGE). Join: ctlm_id
      where the replica exposes it; SCHED_TABLE + JOB_MEM_NAME fallback;
      MEMNAME never a key. Supplement loader itself still unbuilt.

  - id: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_hist_vw"
    system: psgmgr
    origin: controlm
    artifact: cm_hist_vw
    artifact_kind: view
    taxonomy_category: Pipelines
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: ADS
    feeds_taxonomy: []
    adapter: ~
    confirmed: false                    # planned run-history feed (jobrun-observation mapping, status proposed); no extractor/loader yet
    notes: >
      Run history (DTSREMGR retired; JOB_MEM_NAME = JOB_NAME is the only
      reliable join back to CM_DEF_VJOB — MEMNAME is junk, never a key).
      Registered at the N9 build because the v2 grain finally has a row for
      the jobrun-observation mapping to cite; expensive view — every extract
      must bind an indexed predicate.

  - id: "seal@[db].psgmgr.cm_escalation_db"
    system: psgmgr
    origin: seal
    artifact: cm_escalation_db
    artifact_kind: table
    taxonomy_category: ITSM / Gov
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: ADS
    feeds_taxonomy: []
    adapter: ~
    confirmed: false                    # future feed — no extractor/loader; registered because it is the gate's own worked example of a replica (origin seal, carrier psgmgr)
    notes: >
      Escalation/SCIM routing (EJOBNAME join, ECOMPONENT = SEAL). The user's
      named case for the replica grammar: SEAL data landing in psgmgr is a
      SEAL dataset ON a psgmgr carrier, not "a psgmgr table".

  # ---- Control-M born-here export --------------------------------------------
  - id: "controlm:deftable-xml-export"
    system: controlm
    origin: controlm
    artifact: deftable-xml-export
    artifact_kind: file
    taxonomy_category: Pipelines
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: SOR
    feeds_taxonomy: [folders, jobs, variables]
    adapter: ~                          # G47 extractor (drydocs_lineage/extractors/controlm_xml.py) — taxonomy-first staging, no loader
    locator:
      data_root: "DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT (default ~/data/DryDocs); controlm-xml/ = definition exports (arbitrarily-named .xml — landing-zone convention + classification are the guard)"
      resolver: drydocs_core/data_root.py   # controlm_xml_dir() (the G19 shared helper)
    confirmed: false                    # OPEN precedence ruling vs the psgmgr replica datasets (HITL — IDEAS question 2026-07-29); NOTHING writes the graph before it
    replaces: controlm-xml-export
    notes: >
      The environment's real config SoR (XML-not-JSON): definitions + ordered
      folder/job variables in one self-consistent snapshot (G47, ASSUMED
      element contract from SYNTHETIC fixtures). Feeds G48
      resolve-cmdline-staging through the ONE shared resolver. Which source
      wins per object vs the psgmgr replica is the open precedence.yaml
      ruling with a named owner-and-sunset (guardrail 3).

  # ---- Orchestrator placeholders (crosswalk-only activations) ----------------
  - id: "autosys:export"
    system: autosys
    origin: autosys
    artifact: export
    artifact_kind: file
    taxonomy_category: Pipelines
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: SOR
    feeds_taxonomy: [folders, jobs, conditions, dependencies]
    adapter: ~
    crosswalk: config/crosswalks/autosys-to-bmc.yaml
    gate_spec: config/gate-prompts/autosys-crosswalk.yaml
    confirmed: true                     # gate autosys-crosswalk SIGNED OFF 2026-07-14 (13 confirmations) — transfers per Q6; loader still unbuilt + separately gated
    replaces: autosys-export
    notes: >
      Crosswalk CONFIRMED (row 6 demoted exact -> approximate at the SME
      wording review). Source-row activation ONLY: no export feed exists and
      no loader is built. Narrative: external/orchestration/autosys/README.md.

  - id: "airflow:dag-export"
    system: airflow
    origin: airflow
    artifact: dag-export
    artifact_kind: file
    taxonomy_category: Pipelines
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: SOR
    feeds_taxonomy: [folders, jobs, conditions, dependencies]
    adapter: ~
    crosswalk: config/crosswalks/airflow-to-bmc.yaml
    gate_spec: config/gate-prompts/airflow-crosswalk.yaml
    confirmed: true                     # gate airflow-crosswalk SIGNED OFF 2026-07-14 (17 confirmations) — transfers per Q6; loader still unbuilt + separately gated
    replaces: airflow-mwaa
    notes: >
      Crosswalk CONFIRMED (row 8 split 8a/8b/8c at the SME wording review).
      Source-row activation ONLY: no DAG-export feed exists. Narrative:
      external/orchestration/airflow/README.md.

  # ---- SEAL --------------------------------------------------------------------
  - id: "seal:app-extract"
    system: seal
    origin: seal
    artifact: app-extract
    artifact_kind: report
    taxonomy_category: Software / Apps
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: SOR
    feeds_taxonomy: [applications, ports, memberships, roles, employees]
    adapter: csv                        # CsvAdapter (samples) / internal extract in prod
    locator:
      mapping: config/source-mappings/seal-extract.yaml   # column ledger (S3; gate business-application-identity §B1(c))
    confirmed: true                     # live since the M1 chain; transfers per Q6
    replaces: seal-extract
    notes: >
      Live. SEAL applications + ownership. The column ledger landed 2026-08-01 (S3)
      as the gate's replacement for the withdrawn per-node id_authority: it records
      that the source's `Application ID` column is what :BusinessApplication.app_id
      is keyed on. DECLARATIVE only (§B6) — no loader reads it. Both
      seal_applications.py and seal_contacts.py bind to this dataset id.

  # ---- PAT (the T19 naming ruling: neither legacy string survives) -----------
  - id: "pat:product-catalog"
    system: pat
    origin: pat
    artifact: product-catalog
    artifact_kind: report
    taxonomy_category: Product
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: SOR
    feeds_taxonomy: [lob, product_lines, products, area_products, dev_teams]
    adapter: csv
    locator:
      extract: ~                        # real report path/export coordinates — internal/ twin only
    confirmed: true                     # catalog-hierarchy gates (SME 2026-06-21 rulings; C9 2026-07-18) — transfers per Q6
    replaces: catalog-pat
    notes: >
      The catalog hierarchy feed (LOB→Product→Team; lowest precedence
      authority). C17 (2026-08-01): this is the ID-CARRYING side — every grain
      (LoB, Sub-LoB, Product Line, Product, Area Product) has a numeric id at
      source, and the hierarchy loaders key on those ids, never on names. The
      product-line rows must come from an extract AT that grain; the sibling
      pat:people-report projects product lines as names only and cannot feed
      them. Sub-LoB is a real source grain we do not model yet (ontology
      decision — see the parked company-catalog back-flow item).
      T19 ruling 2026-07-31: named pat:product-catalog —
      industry-standard naming matching NEITHER legacy string (catalog-pat /
      pat-catalog), so neither repo's wrong value survives; recorded in the
      docs/port-prompt.md divergence ledger for the company T19 gate.

  - id: "pat:people-report"
    system: pat
    origin: pat
    artifact: people-report
    artifact_kind: report
    taxonomy_category: People & Org
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: SOR
    feeds_taxonomy: [team_applications]
    adapter: csv
    locator:
      mapping: ~                        # team report: team_id, lob, seal_ids (1..n), jira board, team_type/relationship, status, agile framework — REAL rows never committed here
    confirmed: true                     # C9 gate (2026-07-18): the PAT team report as the team_applications feed — transfers per Q6
    replaces: catalog-pat
    notes: >
      The PAT team report (split out of the old catalog-pat umbrella — the
      forced-split example). Team-scoped seal_ids populate the ACTIVE
      arch_develops edge; alignment (supporting area product, else product)
      is VOLATILE and relationship-typed (dedicated|aligned|flex), swept per
      team on each load. SME evidence held in-session (confidential).
      C17 (2026-08-01): this report carries ID+Name for Product / Supporting
      Area Product / Sponsoring Area Product / Sponsoring Product, but projects
      Product Line and Sponsoring Product Line as NAMES ONLY. That is a report
      projection, not a source limitation — the ids exist upstream. It therefore
      feeds team alignment and never the product-line grain; Sponsoring Product
      Line stays unmodelled while it is name-only.

  # ---- ServiceNow (Q4 — registers now, typed SaaS) ---------------------------
  - id: "snow:cmdb-ci-classes"
    system: snow
    origin: snow
    artifact: cmdb-ci-classes
    artifact_kind: file
    taxonomy_category: ITSM / Gov
    asset_type: dcat:Dataset
    authority: SOR

# =============================================================================
# config/audit-fields.yaml — per-source SOURCE AUDIT ENVELOPE mapping (doc 06).
#
# THE ENVELOPE: four frozen node-property names that carry source authorship —
#   source_created_by / source_created_at / source_updated_by / source_updated_at
# — mapped per source from that source's NATIVE audit columns. This answers
# "who created / last changed this thing IN THE SOURCE, and when" — distinct
# from pull tracking (first_seen_at / last_seen_at / last_run_id = when WE saw
# it) and from PROV load provenance (:JobRun edges).
#
# HITL RULE (doc 06 Phase 0): every entry's column→envelope mapping is decided
# at an SME gate before a loader may SET the properties — `status: confirmed`
# + `decided_by` (gate id in config/gate-log.md). `status: stub` marks a
# registered source whose envelope gate has not run; loaders must not write
# envelope properties for stub sources.
#
# Ontology note: the envelope properties are property-level provenance —
# standard terms dct:creator / dct:created / dct:modified (Dublin Core) or
# PROV qualified attribution. Property-term binding is NOT yet registered
# (relationship_vocabulary.yaml covers edges only) — tracked in IDEAS.
#
# classification: Internal-Public — mechanism only (column names + rules; the
# column names below are vendor-schema mechanism). Confidential sources keep
# their real column mappings in the internal twin (same split as the planned
# source-mappings ledger, doc 08); their entries here stay `stub`.
#
# Guarded by tests/unit/test_audit_fields.py: schema, frozen envelope prop
# names, every confirmed:true source in config/source-registry.yaml has an
# entry, confirmed entries map only envelope properties.
# =============================================================================
schema: drydocs.audit-fields.v1
classification: Internal-Public
updated: 2026-07-31                    # N9: re-keyed to the v2 dataset ids (gate source-registry-v2; Q6 transfers)

# The four envelope property names, frozen (test-enforced).
envelope:

  - source_created_at
  - source_updated_by
  - source_updated_at

sources:

    decided_by: controlm-q1q3-phase1         # SME gate 2026-07-07 (config/gate-log.md)

      - object: CM_DEF_VJOB                  # -> :ControlMJob
        mapping:
          source_created_by: CREATION_USER
          source_created_at: CREATION_DATE
          source_updated_by: CHANGE_USERID
          source_updated_at: CHANGE_DATE
        excluded:
          - {column: VERSION_USER,      reason: "current-version duplicate of CHANGE_USERID (gate Q2)"}
          - {column: VERSION_TIMESTAMP, reason: "current-version duplicate of CHANGE_DATE (gate Q2)"}
          - {column: CAPTURE_DATE,      reason: "replication time — never authorship"}
        notes: >
          AUTHOR is the Control-M team's Functional ID, not an individual editor
          (SME 2026-07-06) — stays a plain property, not envelope. Derived
          employee_sid (strip trailing 'p' from *_USER) approved at the gate but

          source_updated_by: LAST_UPDATED_USER
          source_updated_at: LAST_UPDATED
        excluded:
          - {column: CAPTURE_DATE, reason: "replication time — never authorship"}
        notes: >
          Updated-side only; raw-named last_updated/last_updated_user props are

          controlm_folders.cypher.

  # Newly per-row-visible psgmgr datasets (v2 split, N9): their crosswalk
  # gates signed (q1q3 / hosts-topology / avg-run) but the ENVELOPE gate never

surfaces.title: Precedence
surfaces.content:
# =============================================================================
# config/precedence.yaml — source-of-truth ordering for the configuration layer.
#
# When sources disagree about what something IS, resolve top-down. The first
# authority that has an opinion wins; lower authorities become aliases
# (skos:closeMatch / recorded note), never silent overrides.
#
# Edit `order:` to change which authority is consulted first. The HITL gate
# surfaces every conflict this file resolves so the SME can confirm.
# =============================================================================

schema: drydocs.precedence.v1
updated: 2026-07-15   # K4 clause 7 — seal-pat-source-of-record wired into the live chain

# The ordered authority chain. Lower index = higher authority.
order:
  - id: bmc-baseline
    authority: 1
    role: orchestration-vendor-baseline
    governs: [Folder, Job, Condition, dependency, calendar, execution-host, run-as-user]
    source: external/orchestration/bmc-controlm/
    rationale: >
      BMC Control-M is the canonical orchestrator. Its object semantics are ground truth;
      other orchestrators (AutoSys, Airflow) crosswalk TO these concepts.

  - id: internal-standards
    authority: 2
    role: company-convention
    governs: [naming, data-center-codes, folder-naming, calendar-resolution, description-fields]
    source: knowledge/standards/
    rationale: >
      Company conventions that refine the baseline for our environment. They normalize and
      disambiguate baseline values but do not redefine baseline concepts.

  - id: seal-pat-source-of-record
    authority: 3
    role: internal-source-of-record

      IDENTITY — when a scraped SEAL/PAT fact conflicts with the catalog/PAT taxonomy on what
      an internal application/product IS (not who owns it), SEAL/PAT wins. Placed ABOVE
      lob-product-team because its identity claims must beat the catalog's; ownership/

surfaces.title: Sensitivity classification
surfaces.content:
# =============================================================================
# config/classification.yaml — sensitivity classification (the THIRD axis).
#
# DryDocs ingestion carries three independent axes:
#   (1) precedence authority — which source wins on conflict   (config/precedence.yaml)
#   (2) provenance tier       — TRUST: vendor's words vs Claude inference
#                               (VERBATIM / GROUNDED / SYNTHESIZED, decided at
#                                ingestion, recorded in each SOURCE-MANIFEST)
#   (3) sensitivity classification — THIS file: who may see it / may it be published
#
# The classification is DECIDED AT INGESTION TIME and recorded per source. It drives
# the GitHub publish boundary (PUBLISH-BOUNDARY.md) like a .gitignore: the
# non-publishable tiers never enter a public push.
# =============================================================================

schema: drydocs.classification.v1
updated: 2026-07-31        # J23: Internal-Confidential collapsed into Internal (3 levels; a 4th tier can return if a real handling difference ever materializes)

levels:
  - id: External
    rank: 0
    publishable: true
    description: >
      Publicly available third-party material — vendor docs fetched from a public URL,
      ontology standards, academic research.
    homes: [reference/, external/]
    requires: [source_url, captured_at]      # External => must cite the public URL + fetch date

  - id: Internal-Public                       # "Internal-Public Availability"
    rank: 1
    publishable: true
    description: >
      Internally authored but cleared for public availability — design prose, ontology
      docs, generic naming standards. Contains no confidential identifiers.
    homes: [knowledge/]

  - id: Internal
    rank: 2
    publishable: false
    description: >
      Internal-only — NOT for public GitHub, never leaves the private repo. Operational
      metadata, internal process docs, AND confidential material (real rosters, SIDs,
      SEAL ids, schema object names) — the former Internal-Confidential tier collapsed
      into this level (user ruling 2026-07-31, J23): the private repo + publish boundary
      is the protection, and the extra tier's pointer-never-the-data discipline was
      preventing internal/ from holding the values the work needs. Where a source is
      confidential, say so in a handling note on the entry. Real secrets/credentials
      still never commit anywhere; large or PII-bearing payloads may stay out-of-tree
      per source (noted on the entry), no longer tier-forced.
    homes: [internal/]

# The GitHub publish boundary (a .gitignore-style guard).
publish_rule:
  publish_when: "level.publishable == true"            # External + Internal-Public
  exclude_from_public_push: [Internal]
  enforced_by: "PUBLISH-BOUNDARY.md (+ .gitignore on the public remote)"
  note: >
    The directory layout aligns with this — reference/ + external/ + knowledge/ are
    publishable; internal/ is not — but the per-source `classification` label is the
    authoritative driver of what is excluded from a public push.

# Required on EVERY ingested source (a data feed OR a document corpus).
required_on_every_source:
  - classification      # one of levels[].id — in config/source-registry.yaml (feeds)
                        #   and in each SOURCE-MANIFEST (document corpora)
  - source              # the system/path the data came from (e.g. oracle:psgmgr)
required_for_external:  # additionally, when classification == External:
  - source_url          # the public URL the content was fetched from
  - captured_at         # the ingestion / fetch date

# NB: this axis is SENSITIVITY, not TRUST. The provenance tier
# (VERBATIM/GROUNDED/SYNTHESIZED) lives in each SOURCE-MANIFEST and answers a
# different question (is this the vendor's words or Claude's inference?).

# Publish ceiling — ce-wilson/DryDocs is PRIVATE (verified via gh, 2026-07-18;
# an earlier revision of this comment wrongly said "public") but SOMETIMES
# PUBLISHED (CLAUDE.md §3), so treat every tracked file as publishable-eventually:
# Internal-Public stays the maximum tier for tracked files; everything Internal or
# above lives in a gitignored twin (drydocs/data/ etc.).
# drydocs/data/samples/** is synthetic-only (no standing exceptions). The two
# pre-boundary seal_*__sample.csv twins (tracked 2026-05-18, real seal_ids with
# fictional names) were DELETED from the tip 2026-07-19 (user call); git HISTORY
# retains them until a history rewrite — the residual reason any public
# publication of this repo's history remains user-gated.
public_producer:
  ceiling_tier: Internal-Public
  flow: one-way               # public → internal; never pulled back via git

# Sanitization map — how to demote a higher-tier value to Internal-Public so a
# doc or fixture can be committed to this repo.
sanitize:
  real_seal_or_app_id:   "<seal-id> / <app-id>"
  real_lob_product_name: "<LoB> or a generic role (e.g. 'a cards LoB')"
  real_system_codename:  "generic functional name (e.g. 'Business Catalog')"
  real_infra_object:     "placeholder or synthetic example"
  roster_row:            "synthetic name, or omit"
  internal_ghe_repo_id:  "<internal-ghe>"
  real_location_row:     "synthetic or omit"

# Paths that are Internal-only regardless of content — never port outward.
excluded_paths:
  - ".github/skills/**"
  - ".vscode/**"
  - "drydocs/data/**"              # gitignored — real source/sample data + internal twins
  - "stg_out/"                     # gitignored — extract/staging output (real data)
  - "stg_*/"
  - "team_locations__sample.csv"   # real location rows, even if non-PII
  - "docs/design/feedback/scans/**"  # gitignored — raw paper-HITL scans (Epic L / L6);
                                      # Internal by default, see scans/README.md; the
                                      # ANCHOR-KEYED TRANSCRIPTION derived from a scan
                                      # (docs/design/feedback/<doc>-rev<N>.yaml) is a
                                      # separate, publishable-by-default artifact — not
                                      # covered by this exclusion

surfaces.title: Taxonomy <-> Ontology map
surfaces.content:
# =============================================================================
# config/taxonomy-ontology-map.yaml — the HITL-confirmed bridge.
#
# THE central artifact of the configuration layer. Each entry says:
#   "this imported TAXONOMY element  →  apply THIS ONTOLOGY rule."
#
# Lifecycle of every entry:
#   proposed   → ontology-mapper drafted it from the PROV matrix
#   confirmed  → SME approved via the guided gate (docs/restructure/03-hitl-sme-flow.md)
#   applied    → a loader has written it to the graph
#   rejected   → SME declined; kept for audit, never loaded
#
# A taxonomy NEVER becomes graph edges until its mapping is `confirmed`.
# This is the fix for the POC drift (relationships that ignored taxonomy/ontology).
# =============================================================================

schema: drydocs.taxonomy-ontology-map.v1
updated: 2026-07-27                        # +business-application-identity (S3 gate SIGNED OFF — property binding, no edge); prior 2026-07-22: +app-code-defined-mapping, +dl-contact-point (both proposed — attribution close-out + email-DL gates); prior: C12/C13 requires-scheduler rejected (platforms-taxonomy gate)

mappings:

  # ---- Example: a confirmed orchestration mapping (already live) -----------
  - id: job-contains
    taxonomy:
      source: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_def_vjob"
      element: "Folder contains Job"      # raw classification from the import
    ontology:
      from_node: ControlMFolder                 # prov:Collection
      to_node: ControlMJob                 # prov:Activity
      prov_type_from: Collection
      prov_type_to: Activity
      matrix_row: "Collection → any = prov:hadMember"
      neo4j_label: CONTAINS_JOB            # domain alias mapping to hadMember
      prov_maps_to: "prov:hadMember"
    precedence_authority: bmc-baseline
    status: applied
    applied_on: 2026-06-09
    confirmed_by: "(seed)"
    confirmed_on: 2026-06-09

  # ---- 2026-07-07 gate: Q1–Q3 resolutions (controlm-q1q3-phase1) ------------
  - id: application-contains-folder
    taxonomy:
      source: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_def_vtab"
      element: "Control-M APPLICATION groups folders (CM_DEF_VJOB.APPLICATION — NOT the business application)"
    ontology:
      from_node: ControlMApplication            # prov:Collection (new label, this gate)
      to_node: ControlMFolder                   # prov:Collection
      prov_type_from: Collection
      prov_type_to: Collection
      matrix_row: "Collection → any = prov:hadMember"
      neo4j_label: CONTAINS_FOLDER
      prov_maps_to: "prov:hadMember"
    precedence_authority: bmc-baseline
    vocab_id: m3_contains_folder
    status: applied                             # loader: controlm_folders.cypher (folder-pass header-row join)
    applied_on: 2026-07-07
    confirmed_by: SME
    confirmed_on: 2026-07-07

  # ---- C1: Control-M edges (reuse ACTIVE vocabulary terms — batch-confirm) --
  # Source taxonomy: config/taxonomy/controlm.yaml. Each reuses an existing
  # `status: active` entry in relationship_vocabulary.yaml (the mature M3 model),
  # so the matrix row + node classifications are already confirmed — no new terms.

  - id: folder-scheduled-on
    taxonomy:
      source: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_def_vtab"
      element: "Folder is scheduled on a Control-M server (data center)"
    ontology:
      from_node: ControlMFolder                 # prov:Collection

      prov_type_from: Collection
      prov_type_to: "n/a (infrastructure)"
      matrix_row: "no PROV row — infrastructure placement"

    precedence_authority: bmc-baseline
    vocab_id: m3_scheduled_on

  - id: job-requires-in-condition
    taxonomy:
      source: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_def_lnki_p_vw"
      element: "Job requires a named IN condition before it runs"
    ontology:
      from_node: ControlMJob               # prov:Activity
      to_node: Condition                   # prov:Entity
      prov_type_from: Activity
      prov_type_to: Entity
      matrix_row: "Activity → Entity = prov:used"
      neo4j_label: REQUIRES_IN_CONDITION   # domain alias mapping to prov:used
      prov_maps_to: "prov:used"
    precedence_authority: bmc-baseline
    vocab_id: m3_requires_in_condition
    status: confirmed
    confirmed_by: SME
    confirmed_on: 2026-06-21

  - id: job-emits-out-condition
    taxonomy:
      source: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_def_lnko_p_vw"
      element: "Job emits a named OUT condition on completion (SIGN +/-)"
    ontology:
      from_node: ControlMJob               # prov:Activity
      to_node: Condition                   # prov:Entity
      prov_type_from: Activity
      prov_type_to: Entity
      matrix_row: "Activity → Entity = prov:generated"
      neo4j_label: EMITS_OUT_CONDITION     # domain alias mapping to prov:generated
      prov_maps_to: "prov:generated"
    precedence_authority: bmc-baseline
    vocab_id: m3_emits_out_condition
    status: confirmed
    confirmed_by: SME
    confirmed_on: 2026-06-21

  - id: job-was-informed-by
    taxonomy:
      source: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_def_lnki_p_vw"   # the IN⋈OUT pairing's anchor dataset (see the dataset row's note)
      element: "Successor job depends on predecessor via shared OUT→IN condition (derived)"
    ontology:
      from_node: ControlMJob               # prov:Activity (successor)
      to_node: ControlMJob                 # prov:Activity (predecessor)
      prov_type_from: Activity
      prov_type_to: Activity

      prov_maps_to: "prov:wasInformedBy"
    precedence_authority: bmc-baseline
    vocab_id: m3_was_informed_by
    status: confirmed
    confirmed_by: SME
    confirmed_on: 2026-06-21

  # ---- K1: SEAL application attribution (PROPOSED — registration before the gate) --
  # Source: 2026-07-01 company reconciliation (SME-reviewed at source; spec-level on
  # both repos here — no loader, no supplement, no gate log yet). Activation is K2.

  - id: job-seal-app-ref
    taxonomy:
      source: controlm-variable-normalization
      element: "Job is attributed to its SEAL-registered application (fact_type SEAL)"
    ontology:
      from_node: ControlMJob                # prov:Activity
      to_node: BusinessApplication                  # prov:SoftwareAgent (SEAL-registered)
      prov_type_from: Activity
      prov_type_to: Agent
      matrix_row: "Activity → Agent = prov:wasAssociatedWith"
      neo4j_label: WAS_ASSOCIATED_WITH
      role: seal_app_ref
      prov_maps_to: "prov:wasAssociatedWith"
    precedence_authority: bmc-baseline
    vocab_id: m3_seal_app_ref
    source_evidence: "STG_APP_FACT semantic facts (fact_type SEAL), fed by the Control-M variable-normalization stream (config/source-registry.yaml); NEVER raw job.APPLICATION — documented unreliable for SEAL identity in both repos' loader comments."
    capture: >
      waived — no config/taxonomy/ capture file exists for the controlm-variable-normalization
      stream (the F5 taxonomy-first gap, docs/reviews/tech-debt-taxonomy-ontology-map.md); its
      registration lives in config/source-registry.yaml. Retrofitting a capture is a
      taxonomy-importer task — recorded here, not guessed.
    status: confirmed                       # gate seal-attribution-match-policy SIGNED OFF (match policy; edge shape re-opens with K4, see type_conflict_note)
    confirmed_by: chad.wilson
    confirmed_on: 2026-07-14
    provenance_note: "2026-07-01 company reconciliation; spec-level on both repos; producer registration K1, activation K2. Match policy confirmed 2026-07-14 while :BusinessApplication is still prov:SoftwareAgent (K3 reclass unapplied); the K4 reclass re-opens the edge SHAPE per the K3 §F deferral — the confirmed policy itself is shape-agnostic."
    open_questions:
      - "ANSWERED 2026-07-14 (gate): one-to-one match accepted at the top available tier without further review."
      - "ANSWERED 2026-07-14 (gate): unmatched jobs surface as a per-run coverage count (matched + unmatched = eligible), joins graph_verify; never blocks the run."
      - "ANSWERED 2026-07-14 (gate): deterministic triage accepted as default (most-recent run_id, then lowest seal_id, last resort only); every multi-hit flagged for after-the-fact audit — no per-case load-time SME calls."
    type_conflict_note: >
      2026-07-08 review: this mapping requires :BusinessApplication to be a prov:Agent (matrix row
      Activity -> Agent = prov:wasAssociatedWith). The proposed SEAL reshape
      (application-as-dataproduct, this file) reclasses :BusinessApplication to prov:Entity /
      dprod:DataProduct, which no longer type-checks against wasAssociatedWith. If the reshape
      is confirmed, this mapping must be RE-SHAPED, not carried forward as-is — see
      proposed_reshape below. Still status: proposed; not resolved by this note.
    proposed_reshape: >
      Re-shape the job<->app link as an attribution/domain edge to the app-as-Entity instead of
      wasAssociatedWith. Two candidates, NOT decided: (a) ControlMJob -[:USED]-> Application
      (matrix row Activity -> Entity = prov:used, role=seal_app_ref) if the job is read as
      consuming/referencing the app record; (b) a local domain edge (prov_maps_to: ~) analogous
      to arch_contains_batch / dev-team-develops-app, since "job belongs to this business
      application" reads closer to a containment/ownership fact than a used/consumed fact.
      Flagged for the SME at the same gate that confirms application-as-dataproduct — see
      config/gate-prompts/seal-tom-attribution-reshape.yaml section F (K2 re-shape).

  # ---- REQUIRES_SCHEDULER (backlog C6, 2026-07-09) — REJECTED/superseded at C12 ----

    taxonomy:
      source: "seal:app-extract"
      element: "A BatchProcessing data port requires a scheduler technology (which orchestrator runs its batch)"
    ontology:
      from_node: Port                       # as registered; the pre-gate HOIST direction was absorbed by the reg_uses_software landing (that edge is app-level already), so no reshape ever applied
      to_node: SchedulerKind                # RETIRED TARGET — deprecated at C12 (seeds retired in ontology.cypher; the scheduler_kind constraint was then REMOVED 2026-07-23 in the C13 leftover sweep — pre-C13 graphs are wiped and rebuilt from bootstrap, so nothing creates or holds the label). The fact lands on the ACTIVE registry edge (:BusinessApplication)-[:USES_SOFTWARE {source: 'batch-port'}]->(:SoftwareProduct {role: orchestrator}) — reg_uses_software
      prov_type_from: Entity                # dprod port (Entity semantics)
      prov_type_to: ~                        # moot — the entry retired before a target class was ever settled
      matrix_row: "n/a — infrastructure/capability placement, no PROV row (same family as SCHEDULED_ON)"
      neo4j_label: REQUIRES_SCHEDULER
      role: ~
      prov_maps_to: ~
    precedence_authority: bmc-baseline
    vocab_id: seal_requires_scheduler
    source_evidence: "README.md:263 + docs/history/LoadPlanV3.md:82,393 (documented as a post-load edge); never wired — the vocab entry stayed planned until its 2026-07-21 deprecation."
    status: rejected                         # SUPERSEDED, not repudiated: C12 platforms-taxonomy gate (SIGNED OFF 2026-07-21 pm, B1; config/gate-log.md) ruled the orchestrator fact lands on reg_uses_software {source: 'batch-port'} — this proposed edge is never loaded; kept for audit (the rejected lifecycle). Loader migration = backlog C14.
    confirmed_by: chad.wilson                # who/when the closure was ruled (the gate sign-off)
    confirmed_on: 2026-07-21

    gate_spec: config/gate-prompts/platforms-taxonomy.yaml
    provenance_note: "Registered per backlog C6 (2026-07-09) to close the README/LoadPlanV3-vs-vocab drift. Edge meaning ⇒ HITL gate; not auto-decided. CLOSED at C12 (2026-07-21): superseded by reg_uses_software; resolutions below."
    open_questions:                          # ALL CLOSED at C12 (2026-07-21) — kept as the question-by-question audit record
      - "RESOLVED (1) Attach point: the reg_uses_software landing is app-level ((:BusinessApplication)-[:USES_SOFTWARE]->) — the pre-gate HOIST direction is satisfied by the landing edge itself; no :Port reshape ever applied. Batch-only survives as the source value: source: 'batch-port' names the batch port as where the fact comes from."

      element: "BusinessApplication (SEAL-registered) is a data-product/asset record, not a software agent"
    ontology:

      to_node: ~                            # node reclassification, not an edge
      current_class: "prov:SoftwareAgent"
      proposed_class: "prov:Entity / dprod:DataProduct"
      prov_type_from: Agent

        is the precise fit, and it is also the type prov:hadPrimarySource (Entity -> Entity)
        requires of the source-of-record edge (seal-doc-source-of-record below).
    precedence_authority: lob-product-team
    standards_cited: ["PROV-O (prov:Entity)", "DPROD/EKGF (dprod:DataProduct)"]
    vocab_id: ~                             # node reclass, not an edge — see relationship_vocabulary.yaml node_classifications#BusinessApplication (reclass APPLIED)
    capture: config/taxonomy/business-application.yaml
    status: applied
    proposed_at: 2026-07-08
    confirmed_by: SME
    confirmed_on: 2026-07-10                # gate §A + label decision (gate-log)
    applied_on: 2026-07-15                  # K4 clause 1 — reclass + :BusinessApplication label across schema/loaders/tests
    resolved_questions:
      - "K1/K2 job->app edge reshape: DEFERRED by the gate (§F) to a K2 follow-up gate — the standing rider on m3_seal_app_ref / job-seal-app-ref, unchanged by K4."

  - id: seal-tom-attribution

DISTINCT from :Role (org:Role, PAT hierarchy only)."
      vocab_id: [seal_qualified_attribution, seal_attribution_has_agent, seal_attribution_had_role]   # seal_app_attributed_to_employee stays planned (simple form optional/derivable, gate §B)

  # ---- E1: SOSA/SSN jobrun-observation — GATE PREP (SME NOT present) --------
  # SOSA registration (E1 registration step) is already done: sosa/ssn prefixes in
  # drydocs_core/ontology/namespaces.py, terms seeded in sosa_experimental_supplement.cypher
  # (opt-in, experimental), and the 4 context relationships below registered

  # no graph write.
  - id: jobrun-observation
    taxonomy:
      source: "controlm@[db].psgmgr.cm_hist_vw"   # the run-history view got its own v2 dataset row at N9
      element: "Job execution produced a run with a status at a time (run-history source: psgmgr CM_HIST_VW)"
    ontology:
      from_node: ControlMJobRun            # planned execution node (prov:Activity)
      to_node: ControlMJob                 # the feature of interest (prov:Activity / sosa:FeatureOfInterest)
      pattern: "SOSA observation"
      sosa_mapping:
        feature_of_interest: ControlMJob
        observed_property: "run-status | run-duration | freshness"
        result_time: "resultTime"
      neo4j_label: OBSERVES                 # registered: sosa_observes (status planned)
      sosa_maps_to: "sosa:hasFeatureOfInterest"
      prov_maps_to: ~                       # SOSA, not PROV — record separately
    precedence_authority: bmc-baseline
    adoption: experimental                  # SOSA/SSN is W3C but NOT a declared company standard
    status: proposed                        # <-- gate not yet run; SME was absent when this was drafted
    source_mechanism: >
      Run-history source = psgmgr CM_HIST_VW (see .claude/skills/controlm-db/references/
      query-cookbook.md §HIST — expensive, materializes before ROWNUM; every extract must
      bind an indexed predicate). Join identity: CM_HIST_VW.JOB_MEM_NAME = CM_DEF_VJOB.JOB_NAME
      — the only reliable link from a run row back to its job definition. MEMNAME is a
      separate CM_DEF_VJOB column, already demoted to informational-only in the q1q3 gate
      (":ControlMJob.memname — may be junk; never a key/join") — it is NEVER used as a join
      key here either.
    resolved:
      - "sosa:* terms now registered in relationship_vocabulary.yaml + sosa_experimental_supplement.cypher (sosa_observes/has_result/made_by_sensor/observed_property), all status planned / adoption experimental. (E1 registration step — done.)"
    decision_for_gate:
      question: >
        Is a Control-M job run itself the sosa:Observation (ControlMJobRun node dual-typed
        with Observation semantics), or is a separate Observation node attached to the run
        (ControlMJobRun stays a pure prov:Activity; a distinct :Observation node points at it)?
      option_a:
        name: "ControlMJobRun IS the Observation (dual-typed node)"
        shape: "(:ControlMJobRun:Observation {…}) -[:OBSERVES]-> (:ControlMJob) ; (:ControlMJobRun:Observation) -[:HAS_RESULT]-> (:Result)"
        prov_reading: >
          ControlMJobRun is already classified prov:Activity (node_classifications; phase-2
          execution-lineage entries p2_instance_of / m3_executed_by depend on it). PROV has no
          rule against an Activity also carrying sosa:Observation semantics — W3C guidance
          commonly aligns sosa:Observation with prov:Activity (an observation IS an activity
          that generates a Result), so dual-typing does not conflict with prov_type: Activity.
        sosa_reading: >
          Matches the SSN pattern most literally — one run row = one observation event. No
          extra node or extra edge between the run and its Observation; cheapest to load and
          query (single hop OBSERVES/HAS_RESULT off the run node the E2 loader already creates).
        tradeoffs: >
          Couples the experimental, opt-in vocabulary onto a node the CORE (non-experimental)
          execution-lineage stream depends on (p2_instance_of, m3_executed_by, EXECUTED_BY). If
          SOSA/SSN adoption is later reversed, the Observation label/edges must be stripped from
          a core-lineage node instead of being dropped as an isolated subgraph.
      option_b:
        name: "Separate :Observation node references the run"
        shape: "(:Observation) -[:OBSERVES]-> (:ControlMJob) ; (:Observation) -[:HAS_RESULT]-> (:Result) ; link Observation → ControlMJobRun NOT YET a registered relationship"
        prov_reading: >
          Keeps ControlMJobRun a clean prov:Activity with zero dependency on the experimental
          vocabulary. The edge from Observation to the specific run it is about does not exist
          in relationship_vocabulary.yaml yet — a 5th term (e.g. local OF_RUN) would need to be
          registered status: planned before this option is loadable.
        sosa_reading: >
          Also SSN-valid — SOSA explicitly allows Observations to exist without a strict
          one-to-one binding to a single Activity notion; a Sensor can emit repeated
          Observations about the same FeatureOfInterest independent of execution-lineage nodes.
        tradeoffs: >
          Fully isolates the experimental subgraph (clean rollback: delete all :Observation
          nodes/edges, core lineage untouched) but requires a 5th vocabulary term AND doubles
          node count per run for no added source information — CM_HIST_VW is already
          one-row-per-run, so a separate node duplicates identity rather than adding meaning.
      recommendation:
        option: A
        rationale: >
          CM_HIST_VW is inherently one-row-per-run; that row already carries everything an
          Observation needs (status, timing, result) and everything a JobRun needs (which job,
          which odate). Splitting it into two nodes recreates one identity as two without new
          information, and adds a join every loader/query would repeat. Option A's rollback
          safety is not materially worse than Option B's: a dual-typed node's experimental
          labels/edges (Observation, OBSERVES, HAS_RESULT, MADE_BY_SENSOR,
          OF_OBSERVABLE_PROPERTY) can be dropped with `REMOVE r:Observation` + edge deletes,
          same effort as deleting Option B's separate node, without touching the underlying
          ControlMJobRun / prov:Activity data. NOT a decision — recommendation only; the SME
          must confirm, edit, or reject at the gate.
    open_questions:
      - "Confirm the modelling choice above (Option A recommended) before the E2 loader is written."
      - "Result cardinality: does CM_HIST_VW emit exactly one row per (job, odate, run attempt), or can retries/reruns produce multiple rows needing a run-attempt discriminator on the node key?"
      - "ObservableProperty scope for the pilot: is 'run-status' alone sufficient for E2, or should duration/freshness load in the same pass?"
      - "Does confirming this mapping imply promoting SOSA/SSN's adoption status generally, or stay scoped to this one pilot edge (adoption: experimental persists either way until a separate company-standard decision)?"

surfaces.content:
# =============================================================================
# relationship_vocabulary.yaml  —  DryDocs relationship registry
#
# SECTION 0 (node_classifications): every node label in the graph mapped to a
#   CURIE that expands via drydocs_core/ontology/namespaces.py. All local labels
#   live under dd: (https://drydocs.local/ontology#).
#
# SECTION 1 (prov_matrix): the 9-row decision table. Stable — do not edit.
#   Pick the row whose from_type/to_type matches your node classifications.
#   The neo4j_label in that row is what you use in Cypher, unless a more
#   specific existing label is already established (see local_relationships).
#
# SECTION 2 (local_relationships): one entry per declared relationship.
#   Add here BEFORE writing any Cypher. Status lifecycle:
#     planned    → declared but loader not yet written
#     active     → supplement + loader both exist
#     deprecated → no longer loaded; data kept in graph
#     removed    → data and code both deleted
#
# Fields:
#   id            unique snake_case identifier
#   neo4j_label   the Cypher relationship type
#   inverse_label target-side display phrasing (SUPPORTS -> "supported by"),
#                 read as "<target> <inverse_label> <source>". PRESENTATIONAL
#                 ONLY (C15, 2026-07-28): changes no direction, type, status,
#                 or semantics; storage stays ONE directed edge; explicitly
#                 not a gate matter. Presence enforced by test_schema.py.
#   role          edge property for disambiguation (null = label is sufficient)
#   from_node     source node label
#   to_node       target node label
#   prov_maps_to  PROV-O term this maps to (null = local-only or non-PROV standard)
#   sosa_maps_to  SOSA/SSN term this maps to (experimental context-graph edges only)
#   note          plain-English description + any gotchas
#   supplement    schema file where LocalRelationship is declared (null = base PROV-O)
#   loader        cypher file that writes this relationship
#   domain        controlm | seal | catalog | architecture | context | all
#   status        planned | active | deprecated | removed
#
# EXPERIMENTAL / early adoption: SOSA/SSN (domain: context) terms are W3C but
# NOT a declared *company* standard. They are seeded only by the opt-in
# sosa_experimental_supplement.cypher and tagged adoption:"experimental" in the
# graph. They use status: planned here until the SME confirms via the gate.
#
# Sync history: updated 2026-06-09 from DryDocs Consolidated Documentation
# (Sections 1–4, 6). Corrections applied during that audit:
#   * Membership was documented as "prov:Membership" — no such class exists in
#     PROV-O. Corrected to org:Membership (matches seal_ontology_supplement).
#   * BusinessSegment: doc says org:FormalOrganization; the catalog supplement
#     says org:Organization. Both are valid ORG classes; org:FormalOrganization
#     is the more precise term and is adopted here. Update the supplement
#     comment when convenient.
#   * RUNS_ON (ControlMFolder→ControlMServer) renamed SCHEDULED_ON; the RUNS_ON
#     label is reassigned to execution-host placement (see m3_runs_on_* below).
#   * Section 4 mermaid edges (develops / owns / stored_in / contains /
#     DEPENDS_ON) pre-date the ontology and are normalized to
#     SCREAMING_SNAKE labels with PROV-O mappings where the matrix allows.
# =============================================================================


# ── SECTION 0: Node classifications ──────────────────────────────────────────
# class       = primary OWL/RDFS class (CURIE resolvable via namespaces.py)
# prov_type   = PROV-O behavioural type used to drive the SECTION 1 matrix
#               (Activity | Entity | Collection | Agent | n/a)
# All dd:* classes must be MERGEd as :OntologyTerm:LocalClass in a supplement.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
node_classifications:

  # — Control-M (M3, active) —
  - label:      ControlMJob
    class:      "dd:ControlMJob"
    prov_type:  Activity
    note:       "Job definition; acts as a prov:Activity at runtime. ontology_supplement.cypher."

  - label:      ControlMFolder
    class:      "dd:ControlMFolder"
    prov_type:  Collection
    note:       "prov:Collection of jobs. ontology_supplement.cypher."

  - label:      ControlMApplication
    class:      "dd:ControlMApplication"
    prov_type:  Collection
    note: >
      Control-M APPLICATION grouping from the folder HEADER ROW in CM_DEF_VJOB
      (JOB_ID=1) — deliberately NOT the business :BusinessApplication / SEAL concept.
      prov:Collection of ControlMFolder (see m3_contains_folder). Written in
      the FOLDER pass. SME gate controlm-q1q3-phase1 (2026-07-07); entry added
      2026-07-09 to close the node_classifications gap (the edge was
      registered without its node). ontology_supplement.cypher.

  - label:      ControlMServer
    class:      "dd:ControlMServer"
    prov_type:  n/a
    note: >
      Local platform/infrastructure class — no W3C equivalent. NOT an Agent:
      edges targeting it cannot use prov:wasAssociatedWith (see p2_deployed_to).
      ontology_supplement.cypher.

  - label:      Condition
    class:      "dd:Condition"
    prov_type:  Entity
    note:       "Named scheduling condition (prov:Entity). ontology_supplement.cypher."

  - label:      JobRun
    class:      "dd:JobRun"
    prov_type:  Activity
    note: >
      Loader-run provenance activity (base ontology). Distinct from
      ControlMJobRun (phase-2 runtime execution) — do not merge the labels.

  # — Control-M phase 2 (planned) —
  - label:      ControlMJobRun
    class:      "dd:ControlMJobRun"
    prov_type:  Activity
    note:       "One actual execution of a ControlMJob, from the Control-M history API."

  - label:      Deployment
    class:      "dd:Deployment"
    prov_type:  Activity
    note:       "CI/CD deployment activity that ships folder XML to a server."

  - label:      Developer
    class:      "prov:Person"
    prov_type:  Agent
    note: >
      Human author from Git blame / change records. Likely the same individual
      as an Employee node (SEAL); reconcile by SID when both feeds are loaded.

  - label:      AppUser
    class:      "prov:SoftwareAgent"
    prov_type:  Agent
    note:       "Service account / FID that jobs run as (EPV, Run-as-User)."

  - label:      Script
    class:      "dd:Script"
    prov_type:  Entity
    note: >
      Invocable artifact (placement JAR + Task-JSON). prov:Entity; also a
      prov:Plan in the wasAssociatedWith(hadPlan) pattern. Finer software
      typing available via swo: if ever required.

  - label:      ETLProcess
    class:      "dd:ETLProcess"
    prov_type:  Activity
    note:       "AWS-side ingestion/transformation workload (Glue / DPL). obi: offers a data-transformation class if a standards mapping is later required."

  - label:      ExecutionHost
    class:      "prov:SoftwareAgent"
    prov_type:  Agent
    note: >
      Agent host / ETL cluster entry point. Classified as SoftwareAgent
      (not pure infrastructure) so that AppUser -[:DELEGATES_TO]->
      ExecutionHost can legally map to prov:actedOnBehalfOf, which requires
      Agent → Agent. Local subclass dd:ExecutionHost.

  - label:      ControlMHostGroup
    class:      "dd:ControlMHostGroup"
    prov_type:  Collection
    note: >
      Gate controlm-hosts-topology CONFIRMED 2026-07-09 (config/gate-log.md): a
      Control-M host group / node group (vendor 6.4.01 poster: CMS_NODGRP;
      replica: psgmgr CM_HOSTS) — the load-balancing set of agent hosts a
      job's NODE_ID can resolve to; the group name may itself be a DNS/LB
      alias. Key (data_center, name); members are ExecutionHost nodes.
      Deliberately NOT named "ControlMGroup": CM_DEF_VJOB.GROUP_NAME
      (ControlMJob.group_name) is the application-group concept — a different
      thing entirely; "host group" is the 9.0.x vendor term.

  - label:      DataSource
    class:      "dcat:Dataset"
    prov_type:  Entity
    note: >
      RETIRED 2026-07-15 (lineage rel vocabulary gate, config/gate-log.md):
      superseded by DataAsset — the READS_FROM edge direction already
      encodes the source role. Kept for audit; no loader ever shipped.
      Was: read-side dataset (source zone + Glue database).

  - label:      DataTarget
    class:      "dcat:Dataset"
    prov_type:  Entity
    note: >
      RETIRED 2026-07-15 (lineage rel vocabulary gate, config/gate-log.md):
      superseded by DataAsset — the WRITES_TO edge direction already
      encodes the target role. Kept for audit; no loader ever shipped.
      Was: write-side dataset (target zone / bucket / partitions).

  - label:      DataAsset
    class:      "dcat:Dataset"
    prov_type:  Entity
    note: >
      Added at the lineage rel vocabulary gate 2026-07-15: the D1 proxy
      shape — a piece of data a process reads or writes (hdfs / s3 /
      hive_table / local_file / Glue table, …), keyed on assetId
      (urn:drydocs:dataasset:{platform}:{namespace}:{name};
      provisioning/02_proxy_constraints.cypher — constrained in all three
      data DBs so the ddall composite joins on it). Replaces the retired
      DataSource / DataTarget pair as the to-node of m3_reads_from /
      m3_writes_to.

  # — SEAL (active) —
  - label:      BusinessApplication
    class:      "prov:Entity"
    dual_class: "dprod:DataProduct"
    prov_type:  Entity
    note: >
      SEAL-registered application (a data-product/asset record). seal_ontology_supplement.cypher.
      RECLASSED + RENAMED (K4, 2026-07-15) per the BusinessApplication entity-reshape gate
      §A + label decision (config/gate-log.md 2026-07-10, SME chad.wilson): was label
      Application, class prov:SoftwareAgent/Agent. The old typing carried three incompatible
      PROV types at once (SoftwareAgent here; dprod:Port children = Entity semantics;
      org:Membership role-holders = Organization semantics). Label :Application →
      :BusinessApplication normalized across vocabulary, schema supplements, loaders,
      constraints (businessapplication_*), and tests in the same K4 change.

  - label:      Employee
    class:      "prov:Agent"
    prov_type:  Agent
    note:       "Person holding a role membership. seal_ontology_supplement.cypher."

  - label:      Membership
    class:      "org:Membership"
    prov_type:  n/a
    note: >
      CORRECTED: consolidated doc listed "prov:Membership", which does not
      exist in PROV-O. The W3C ORG ontology owns this class (org:Membership),
      matching seal_ontology_supplement.cypher. n-ary relation node, not a
      PROV participant.

  - label:      Role
    class:      "org:Role"
    prov_type:  n/a
    note:       "Named role in a membership. seal_ontology_supplement.cypher."

  - label:      Port
    class:      "dprod:Port"
    prov_type:  Entity
    note:       "Data port (EventProcessing / BatchProcessing). dprod namespace is the EKGF working default pending the corporate IRI."

  # — SEAL reshape (ACTIVE at K4, 2026-07-15 — gate 2026-07-10 §B) —
  # (seal_had_primary_source targets :Document — declared ONCE in the docs-corpus section
  # below; the duplicate SEAL-reshape Document entry was merged into it 2026-07-09,
  # tech-debt audit F4 — one label, one classification entry.)

  - label:      Attribution
    class:      "prov:Attribution"
    prov_type:  n/a
    note: >
      ACTIVE (K4, 2026-07-15): reified n-ary node for the SEAL Technical Operating Model (TOM)
      qualified-attribution pattern — BusinessApplication -[:QUALIFIED_ATTRIBUTION]-> Attribution
      -[:HAS_AGENT]-> Employee, Attribution -[:HAD_ROLE]-> TOMRole. Same pattern family as

# ── SECTION 1: Decision matrix ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Step 1: classify your source node (Activity / Entity / Agent / Collection).
# Step 2: classify your target node.
# Step 3: read the neo4j_label. Add a `role` property if the same label is
#         used in multiple contexts (e.g., USED {role: "reads_config"}).
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
prov_matrix:

  - from_type:   Activity
    to_type:     Activity
    prov_term:   "prov:wasInformedBy"
    neo4j_label: WAS_INFORMED_BY
    note: >
      One activity's execution depended on outputs produced by another.
      Examples: ControlMJob waiting on a predecessor job's OUT condition.

  - from_type:   Activity
    to_type:     Entity
    prov_term:   "prov:used"
    neo4j_label: USED
    note: >
      Activity consumed / read an entity. Use role= to distinguish multiple
      uses on the same activity (e.g., role: reads_config vs role: reads_input).

  - from_type:   Activity
    to_type:     Entity
    prov_term:   "prov:generated"
    neo4j_label: GENERATED
    note: >
      Activity produced an entity. Inverse of wasGeneratedBy — use this form
      when the natural edge direction is Activity→Entity (e.g., job emits
      an OUT condition). role= distinguishes multiple output types.

  - from_type:   Activity
    to_type:     Agent
    prov_term:   "prov:wasAssociatedWith"
    neo4j_label: WAS_ASSOCIATED_WITH
    note: >
      Activity linked to an agent (person, software system, org unit).
      role= on the edge records the agent's participation type.

  - from_type:   Entity
    to_type:     Activity
    prov_term:   "prov:wasGeneratedBy"
    neo4j_label: WAS_GENERATED_BY
    note: >
      Entity was produced by an activity. Standard provenance direction —
      edge flows Entity→Activity. Already used by BaseLoader for all nodes.

  - from_type:   Entity
    to_type:     Entity
    prov_term:   "prov:wasDerivedFrom"
    neo4j_label: WAS_DERIVED_FROM
    note: >
      Entity was transformed or computed from another entity.
      Examples: a derived dataset, a report generated from raw data.

  - from_type:   Entity
    to_type:     Agent
    prov_term:   "prov:wasAttributedTo"
    neo4j_label: WAS_ATTRIBUTED_TO
    note: >
      Entity ownership or authorship attributed to an agent.
      Examples: a script owned by a team, a dataset attributed to an app.

  - from_type:   Agent
    to_type:     Agent
    prov_term:   "prov:actedOnBehalfOf"
    neo4j_label: ACTED_ON_BEHALF_OF
    note: >
      Agent delegation — one agent acting for another.
      Examples: a service account acting on behalf of an application.

  - from_type:   Collection
    to_type:     any
    prov_term:   "prov:hadMember"
    neo4j_label: HAD_MEMBER
    note: >
      Collection contains a member entity or activity.
      Examples: ControlMFolder (Collection) contains ControlMJob (Activity).
