surfaces.title: Doc-source registry
surfaces.content:
# =============================================================================
# config/doc-source-registry.yaml — every DOCUMENT corpus, declared once (Q5).
#
# The docmeta ledger (ADR 0006; knowledge/upgrade-plans/docmeta-component.md §1.4):
# where the pipeline registry (config/source-registry.yaml) declares DATA FEEDS,
# this file declares DOC CORPORA — content ingested as Document → Chunk lexical
# graphs (or queued to be). Ids match the pipeline registry where a corpus
# appears in both (bmc-docs, essential-graphrag); the pipeline entry stays the
# feed/adapter/gate record, THIS entry is the doc-governance record.
#
# REQUIRED on every entry (enforced by tests/unit/test_doc_registry.py):
#   classification — config/classification.yaml level (External ⇒ source_url + captured_at)
#   source         — the system/path the corpus comes from
#   connector      — web | filedrop | confluence | sharepoint | teams | email
#   tier           — T1 vendor | T2 internal-platform | T3 product/process | T4 SME-context
#   curation       — the ADR 0006 §4 ladder, FIXED per tier:
#                      T1 → none · T2/T3/T4 → sme-confirm (the +confidential rider retired with the J23 tier collapse 2026-07-31)
#   target_db      — dddocs | ddcontext (ADR 0006 §2; never any other DB)
#   refresh        — manual | on-demand | scheduled(<cron>)
#   trust_default  — VERBATIM | GROUNDED | SYNTHESIZED (per-chunk overrides live in
#                    the corpus SOURCE-MANIFEST where one exists)
#   graph_locator  — how `drydocs docs-verify` finds THIS corpus's nodes (Q7):
#                      match: corpus_id | doc_id | path_prefix | none
#                      value: the parameter that match is compared against
#                    Required because the registry is corpus-keyed and the GRAPH
#                    IS NOT: only the Q13 vendor-docs loader writes corpus_id,
#                    bmc_docs identifies pages by repo-relative path, and
#                    essential_graphrag writes one Document whose doc_id is the
#                    corpus id. Declaring it here keeps the check registry-driven
#                    instead of teaching the verifier three loader shapes.
#                    `match: none` = deliberately NOT on the Document->Chunk
#                    lexical spine; docs-verify reports `unshaped`, never
#                    `missing`, so "never loaded this way" is not read as a defect.
#
# Freshness is gate-preserving (ADR 0006 §4): a sha256 change on refetch
# RE-QUEUES curation — a changed page never silently overwrites confirmed content.
#
# N9 (2026-07-31, gate source-registry-v2): the pipeline-registry twin entries
# for these corpora DROPPED — this file is now each corpus's ONE home, so it
# also carries the pipeline `confirmed:` gate state (the lexical-load gates
# that used to live on the twins). The runtime SourceRegistry unions this
# ledger, so doc loaders still gate through require_confirmed.
# =============================================================================

schema: drydocs.doc-source-registry.v1
updated: 2026-07-31

sources:
  # ---- Currently ingested corpora (backfill, Q5) ----------------------------
  - id: bmc-docs
    classification: External            # public BMC documentation; per-doc URLs in each file header
    source: "external/orchestration/bmc-controlm/controlm-*.md (26 converted BMC pages)"
    source_url: "https://documents.bmc.com/ (per-doc URLs in each file header)"
    captured_at: 2026-06-11
    connector: web
    manifest: external/orchestration/bmc-controlm/SOURCE-MANIFEST.md
    trust_default: GROUNDED             # conversion is mechanical but lossy; per-chunk tier per the manifest rule
    tier: T1
    curation: none
    target_db: dddocs                   # ADR 0006 §2 — demonstrated in `drydocs` today; RE-TARGETS to dddocs at the P4 loader build (idempotent reload, not a migration)
    refresh: manual
    taxonomy_path: technology/orchestration/control-m
    graph_locator:                      # pre-dates corpus_id; pages are identified by their repo path
      match: path_prefix
      value: external/orchestration/bmc-controlm/
    confirmed: true                     # gate bmc-docs-lexical-load SME-accepted 2026-07-08 (config/gate-log.md) — moved here from the dropped pipeline twin (N9)
    notes: >
      The canonical T1 vendor corpus (gate bmc-docs-lexical-load, 2026-07-08 —
      recorded on the pipeline-registry twin entry). Loaded as the ACTIVE
      lexical shape: (:Chunk)-[:PART_OF]->(:Document) + FIRST_CHUNK/NEXT_CHUNK,
      (:Document)-[:DESCRIBES]->(:SoftwareProduct).

  - id: bmc-controlm-utilities
    classification: External            # public BMC documentation; robots.txt allows /supportu/9.0.20/*
    source: "DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT/vendor-docs/bmc-controlm-9.0.20-utilities/pages/ (1016 documents / 1017 TOC nodes, 6.0 MB — OUT of the repo tree)"
    source_url: "https://documents.bmc.com/supportu/9.0.20/help/Main_help/en-US/ (Utilities book; per-topic URLs in the capture manifest)"
    captured_at: 2026-07-31
    connector: web
    manifest: DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT/vendor-docs/bmc-controlm-9.0.20-utilities/capture-manifest.json
    trust_default: VERBATIM             # a scrape is the vendor's OWN words — unlike bmc-docs, which is our lossy paraphrase
    tier: T1
    curation: none                      # T1 ladder (ADR 0006 §4)
    target_db: dddocs
    refresh: on-demand
    taxonomy_path: technology/orchestration/control-m
    graph_locator:                      # the Q13 loader writes corpus_id on :Document/:Chunk/:DocSection
      match: corpus_id
      value: bmc-controlm-utilities
    confirmed: false                    # NOT gated yet — no loader may write from this entry until an SME gate signs the doc-graph shape
    notes: >
      Captured 2026-07-31 by scripts/external_vendor_scrape.py (capture id
      bmc-controlm-9.0.20-utilities): 1017 TOC nodes over 1016 DOCUMENTS,
      6.0 MB, zero failures. The two counts differ by one on purpose — one TOC
      node (`89881.htm#o90021`, "ctl High Availability Server parameters")
      addresses a SECTION of another page via a fragment, so it is a real
      navigation node but not a second document. The manifest carries
      `page` + `anchor` per row so the Q13 loader can build the hierarchy
      faithfully without minting a phantom :Document.
      WHY THE PAYLOAD IS NOT IN THE REPO: a
      verbatim vendor scrape is BMC's copyrighted words, not our summary — the
      external/ServiceNow/extracted/ .gitignore precedent, generalized to the
      out-of-repo data root. What is committed is this entry, the capture id,
      and the scraper; never the pages.
      WHY 9.0.20 AND NOT THE ESTATE'S 9.0.21.300: BMC trimmed the 9.0.21 help
      publication, which carries NO Utilities book at all (6 books / 1,965
      pages vs 9.0.20's 20 books / 3,860). Version-specific details therefore
      need confirming against 9.0.21 before they are treated as estate truth —
      the same standing caveat the hand-converted corpus carries for its
      SaaS-sourced pages, and a per-Document property the loader should carry
      rather than a footnote a reader can miss.
      WHAT IT UNBLOCKS: 258 of the 1017 pages are XML/export/import/definition
      topics — "XML file rules", "Creating an XML file", "XML file validation",
      and the emdef family (defjob / exportdefjob / updatedef / copydefjob /
      deldefjob / duplicatedefjob), each with rules + parameters + examples.
      That is the documented gap behind drydocs_lineage/extractors/controlm_xml.py,
      whose XML contract is currently ASSUMED and defined only by synthetic
      fixtures ("XML schema docs are a known reference gap"). exportdefjob is
      the likely producer of the estate's own exports.

  - id: essential-graphrag
    classification: External            # published Manning/Neo4j-sponsored ebook; PDF is LOCAL-ONLY (root /*.pdf gitignore) — cite source_url, never commit
    source: "Essential-GraphRAG.pdf (repo root, gitignored local copy; Bratanič & Hane, Manning 2025)"
    source_url: "https://www.manning.com/books/essential-graphrag"
    captured_at: 2026-07-14
    connector: filedrop
    manifest: ~                         # no SOURCE-MANIFEST — provenance recorded on the pipeline-registry twin + docs/reviews/essential-graphrag-traversal-experiment.md
    trust_default: GROUNDED             # pdf-extract-grounded-v1: pypdf extraction is mechanical but lossy
    tier: T1
    curation: none
    target_db: ddcontext                # experiment/reference content stays out of ground truth (Q2 decision; ADR 0006 §2 keeps it here)
    refresh: manual
    taxonomy_path: ~                    # a methodology book — deliberately no DESCRIBES / product taxonomy hook
    graph_locator:                      # one Document for the whole book; its doc_id IS the corpus id
      match: doc_id
      value: essential-graphrag
    confirmed: true                     # Q2 groom decision 2026-07-16: pure REUSE of the ACTIVE docs_* vocabulary — covering gate = bmc-docs-lexical-load (moved here from the dropped pipeline twin, N9)
    notes: >
      The Q2 agent-traversal experiment corpus; fed the docmeta P0 benchmark
      verdict (traversal arm). Pattern notes mined from the same book:
      reference/research/essential-graphrag-notes.md (Q1).

  # ---- Queued corpora (registered, not yet ingested) ------------------------
  - id: fcdo-frameworks
    classification: Internal               # confidential handling: real employee names + internal Confluence URLs in the capture (J23 collapse)
    source: "internal/fcdo-reference/*.md (2026-07-30 screenshot transcriptions; live-page scrape target list = the page-ID table in internal/fcdo-reference/README.md)"
    connector: confluence                 # company-network only; scrape supersedes the transcripts
    manifest: ~                           # provenance + gap ledger lives in internal/fcdo-reference/README.md
    trust_default: GROUNDED               # screenshot transcription is faithful but partial; a direct Confluence fetch upgrades to VERBATIM
    tier: T4
    curation: sme-confirm                 # T4 ladder post-J23 (+confidential rider retired with the tier)
    target_db: ddcontext                  # reference/standards content, never ground truth
    refresh: on-demand
    taxonomy_path: ~
    graph_locator:                      # no connector has run — nothing to locate until the confluence fetch exists
      match: none
      value: ~
    confirmed: false                    # crosswalk gate not yet drafted (ALIGNMENT-PLAN Phase 1 / backlog W1) — moved here from the dropped pipeline twin (N9)
    notes: >
      The FCDO firmwide data-publishing frameworks corpus (ontology/taxonomy/
      provenance/ETL standards from the internal governance group). Purpose:
      reference for the FCDO ontology crosswalk
      (internal/fcdo-reference/ALIGNMENT-PLAN.md). Priority recapture targets
      when the confluence connector runs: Descriptive Metadata, Data Quality,
      Data Contracts (DPROD) frameworks + the Taxonomy Framework property
      tables — the known capture holes that block crosswalk sign-off.

  - id: jpmc-reports
    classification: External            # public SEC filings / investor-relations PDFs
    source: "scripts/ingest_jpmc_reports.py (REMOVED 2026-07-22 — one-off script with hardcoded connection, superseded by module loaders; recover via git history if needed. 2 local-only PDFs: annualreport-2024 + mda10k-2024; never committed — the root /*.pdf gitignore precedent)"
    source_url: "https://www.jpmorganchase.com/ir/annual-report (per-doc URLs in the ingest script)"
    captured_at: 2026-06-30             # ingest pipeline committed e419ec7; PDFs fetched for that run
    connector: filedrop
    manifest: ~                         # pre-restructure ingest; provenance lives in the script header (classification/trust declared there)
    trust_default: VERBATIM             # direct text extraction; derived segment metrics are GROUNDED (per the script's own tiering)
    tier: T1
    curation: none
    target_db: ddcontext                # the original ddcontext precedent the Q2 book load cited
    refresh: manual
    taxonomy_path: ~
    graph_locator:                      # :DataAsset slices, NOT Document->Chunk — see notes; reshaping is P4+
      match: none
      value: ~
    confirmed: false                    # no active loader binds here; reshaping onto the lexical spine is a P4+ decision — a future loader gates on this flag (N9)
    notes: >
      The FIRST ddcontext doc ingestion (pre-dates the docmeta plan): JPMC
      annual-report sections as :DataAsset slices seeding the effective-dated
      BusinessSegment context — NOT the lexical Document→Chunk shape. Backfilled

surfaces.title: Dev/test environment names
surfaces.content:
# =============================================================================
# config/dev-environment.yaml — canonical local dev/test infrastructure names
# =============================================================================
# Single source of truth for the names and ports the local dev/test stack uses.
# The .env.example templates (root, agents/, web/) and the run-drydocs skill all
# defer to this file — when the container or ports change, change them HERE and
# refresh the templates, not the other way around.
#
# Contains NO company data and NO secrets (names/ports only; passwords live in
# gitignored .env files, never in a committed file).
schema: drydocs.dev-environment.v1

neo4j:
  # Local Neo4j Enterprise container (EE required — ADR 0002 multi-DB + composite;
  # Aura ruled out 2026-07-06). Provision the topology once after first start:
  # drydocs_core/schema/provisioning/provision.ps1
  container: neo4jtest
  image: neo4j:2026.05.0-enterprise   # store written by 2026.05.0 — cannot downgrade to 5.26
  volume: neo4j-testdata              # -> /data   (the graph; survives container recreation)
  plugins_volume: neo4j-testplugins   # -> /plugins (see `plugins:` below)
  plugins: [apoc, graph-data-science]
  # PLUGINS ARE A MOUNTED VOLUME, NOT `NEO4J_PLUGINS` (fixed 2026-07-28). The env-var
  # form asks the entrypoint to DOWNLOAD each plugin at startup; when that download
  # cannot happen the container starts anyway and the plugin is simply absent — which
  # is exactly what was found: `NEO4J_PLUGINS=[apoc]` was set for weeks while
  # /plugins held only README.txt, so `drydocs bootstrap` refused with "APOC required"
  # and the neo4j-drydocs MCP server could not work. Both jars SHIP INSIDE the image
  # (/var/lib/neo4j/labs for apoc, /var/lib/neo4j/products for GDS) and are version-
  # matched to the server, so populating a named volume from the image needs no network
  # and cannot drift from the server version. Populate + create: see the header of
  # drydocs_core/schema/provisioning/provision.ps1 (guarded by tests/unit/test_dev_environment.py).
  # Requires the procedure allowlists — apoc.*,gds.* in BOTH unrestricted and allowlist.
  ports:
    http: 7474            # browser UI  -> http://localhost:7474
    bolt: 7687            # drivers     -> bolt://localhost:7687
  # Docker can remap host ports (an earlier container, neo4j-drydocs-ee, landed on
  # 7476/7689 — retired 2026-07-23: data migrated into the neo4j-testdata volume and
  # this canonical container recreated on 7474/7687; the old container is kept stopped
  # (restart=no) as a rollback copy). If a connection is refused, trust
  # `docker port <container>` over any template value.
  databases:              # ADR 0002 topology — provisioned, not implicit
    ground_truth: drydocs      # main load + lineage writers; default load target
    lineage: ddlineage         # cross-platform lineage (drydocs_lineage)
    uncertain_context: ddcontext  # SYNTHESIZED/unverified only (drydocs_deepdoc)
    composite: ddall           # read-only federation of all three
  home_db_warning: >
    The EE home database `neo4j` is NOT part of the topology — loading into it
    puts data where no query surface looks. Set NEO4J_DATABASE to a topology
    database (normally `drydocs`).

services:
  # Local dev servers the web UI expects (see web/.env.example).
  adk_api: 8000           # agents ADK server (VITE_ADK_URL)
  drydocs_api: 8001       # thin read API, ADR 0005 (VITE_API_URL)

depgraph:
  # The code-graph INSTRUMENT (U7). knowledge/depgraph-snapshots/snapshot.ps1
  # shells out to this sibling checkout, so the revision here decides what a
  # snapshot can see — it is dev infrastructure exactly like the container above.
  repo: ../depgraph       # sibling of the DryDocs repo root, NOT a submodule
  remote: https://github.com/ce-wilson/depgraph.git
  # FORK CONSOLIDATED 2026-07-28 (depgraph 5006567). It was two divergent
  # siblings off a one-commit main — feat/p0-vector (--tree) and
  # feat/controlm-lineage (the U6 multi-root resolver) — with neither an
  # ancestor of the other, so no revision had everything and a plain clone of
  # `main` reproduced the broken scanner. Both are now merged into main and the
  # branches are DELETED (local + remote); main is the only branch. Track main.
  expected_branch: main
  expected_commit: 5006567
  # What snapshot.ps1 REFUSES to scan without. These are probed behaviourally
  # (knowledge/depgraph-snapshots/probe_instrument.py) rather than by version
  # string — capability is the thing that matters, and depgraph's 0.1.0 spans
  # both the broken and the fixed resolver, so a version says nothing.
  requires:
    scan: [multi_root]    # every run
    tree: [tree]          # additionally, when -Tree is passed
  # Does the live-capability test ASSERT against the checkout, or skip?
  # True producer-side: the sibling is ours, a missing capability is a real defect
  # here, and failing loudly is the entire point of U7. A consumer whose depgraph
  # fork is separately owned — and so cannot be remediated by a port — sets this
  # FALSE with the owed action recorded, and flips it back when the fork catches up
  # (PORT-REPORT-94132c80 / owed action 48e). Deliberately a config flag and NOT an
  # env var or a second test variant: this file is canonical-company in
  # PORT-MANIFEST.yaml, so the divergence lives in the one file already ruled
  # per-side and tests/unit/test_probe_instrument.py stays BYTE-IDENTICAL on both
  # sides — nothing to reconcile at the next port.
  capability_assert: true
